reviewType: AI full sequential semantic assessment and independent second semantic reread; not human review

firstPass.method: Each word and its recorded meaning read in order, with individually authored stage/reason codes.

secondPass.method: Each word, recorded meaning and initial decision reread in order; lexical familiarity, register, school exposure and specialist requirements reconsidered individually.

additionalBasicBandReview.method: All entries remaining in the initial basic band after the full second pass were read together and reconsidered for over-broad Grade 1 assignments; no automatic reassignment.
additionalBasicBandReview.scope: Every then-current stage 0 entry, printed as a complete list.

standards: Classify the written lexical item and recorded sense by earliest reasonable educational exposure, recognition, register and conceptual background.
Stage 0 is the basic Grade 1 core; stage 1 also covers primary grades 2-6; stage 2 also covers middle-school grades 8-9.
No quotas, previous rarity, source frequency, single-character rule or word-length rule used to assign stages.
Common school literary imagery, classical prose vocabulary and ordinary rhetoric remain 1/2 where exposure reasonably supports this.
Modern specialist non-language science, medical, material, engineering, administrative and botanical/zoological vocabulary is at most 3.
Stage 4 is reserved for rare classical lexical senses and specialist language/literature/cultural textual study; familiar underlying objects do not lower archaic lexical names.
Ordinary familiar foods/species and everyday regional words are not automatically technical or classical merely because less familiar to some speakers.
These are practical AI-inferred learning bands, not an official nationwide per-grade list.
boundaries: 铂金 retains 1 because its recorded examples teach ordinary jewelry material, not tertiary chemical properties.
仄声 is 2 for ordinary school prosody; 训诂 and 匚部 are 4 for specialist historical lexical/dictionary knowledge.
圆锥 is 1 for elementary solid geometry; 山峁 is 2 for school landform geography; obscure chemical elements and specific engineering parts are 3.
骐骥、蜉蝣、觥筹、始龀 and similar familiar curricular classical terms are 2; rare lexical alternatives such as 筱竹 and older dawn senses are 4.
怀娠 is 4 for its explicitly ancient lexical pregnancy sense; formal medical disease and anatomical terminology remains at most 3.
Surnames, personal-name characters and place names are differentiated by reasonable lexical recognition and historical usage; neither their name status nor one-character spelling dictates the stage.
